# Independent audit of paired centroid tails and symmetric noise

Audited `candidate 732b11a769399016` in full.
Result: **PASS**. The exact verifier
`supporting computation verify_paired_centroid_tail_scalar_certificates.py` was rerun and passes.
This audit does not infer an OC bound for nonproduct mixed sources.

## 1. Localization and dimensions

The full author-uploaded FG2004 Theorem 2 was independently read in the
earlier `historical context (not an accepted premise)`. Its
parameter range includes the endpoint 1/2. An actual d-dimensional body
has a one-dimensional marginal density with concave 1/(d-1) power,
corresponding to measure parameter 1/d. The localized density is therefore
affine^(d-1). In particular d=2 is covered, without an endpoint limit.

On the fixed compact support interval, the mean inequality is a valid
single continuous integral constraint; the closed-tail sum is affine
and weakly upper semicontinuous. Admissible Diracs contribute at most
one for strictly positive shift. The remaining extremizer is exactly
centered. Its additional one-sided moment condition holds because
every proper initial moment is strictly negative for a nondegenerate
centered interval law. Thus there is no hidden second equality constraint.

## 2. Complete scalar shape reduction

For the increasing affine-power law on [r,1], its mean m is at least
the interval midpoint. Therefore both CDF arguments m-h,m+h stay in
support until h=1-m. On this first interval the paired CDF has derivative
f(m+h)-f(m-h)>=0. On [1-m,m-r] the upper CDF is one and the lower decreases.
Afterwards the sum is one. This proves both its maximum 1+T_d(r) and its
minimum min(2G(m),1), including empty middle intervals.

Reflecting the law changes its paired CDF to 2-H(h); atomlessness makes
this exact at all endpoints. The frustum realizing density t^(d-1) is an
actual d-dimensional convex body, including the r=0 pyramid. Its lower
centroid cap G(m)>=gamma_d therefore follows from ordinary body Grünbaum,
and closes the decreasing branch. Constant affine roots give a uniform
interval and paired sum one.

The d=2 rational formula and d=3 positive-polynomial factorization in
Section 4 were checked by the exact verifier. Both imply precisely the
required bound, with their stated denominators positive for 0<=r<1.

## 3. Logarithmic and quadrature signs

The derivative of

    J(v)=-log v-(1-v)(7+5v)/(2(1+5v))

has the sign of `(v-1)(5v-1)(5v-2)`. Thus J decreases on (0,1/5),
increases on (1/5,2/5), and decreases on (2/5,1]. Its only minimum
candidates are 1/5 and 1. At zero it diverges to infinity. The former
minimum is log5-8/5>0, and the latter is zero. The four-term atanh-series
certificate exceeds 8/5 by exactly 4/15309.

For v=(R+t)/(1+t), a=(1+5R)/6, the log bound is equivalent to

    2 avg_[R,1] 1/(u+t) >= 1/(1+t)+1/(a+t).

The desired rational-kernel quadrature gap is exactly

    1/(1+t)+a/(a+t)-2 avg_[R,1] u/(u+t)
     =t[2 avg_[R,1] 1/(u+t)-1/(1+t)-1/(a+t)]>=0.

Thus no sign reverses when passing to u/(u+t). Its positive Stieltjes
representation has integrable exponents alpha-1 near zero and alpha-2
at infinity for 0<alpha<1. Each averaged or endpoint integral is finite;
Tonelli handles the nonnegative averaging, and there is no subtraction
of divergent expressions. The value u=0 causes no problem.

Taking alpha=1/d and R=r^d identifies the average exactly with m.
Since 2m-1>=r>=0, taking d-th powers preserves the inequality and gives
T_d<=1/6. For every d>=4, monotonicity gamma_d<=gamma_4 and the exact
gap `1-2gamma_4-1/6=53/3750>0` complete the scalar estimate.

## 4. Transfer and closed-boundary cases

The original scalar marginal is atomless, so a paired lower-CDF upper
bound converts exactly to the required paired closed upper-tail lower
bound. For the generalized scalar-measure assertion at shift zero,
one may simply let the positive shift decrease to zero; non-atomicity
gives continuity. For an actual body, ordinary Grünbaum already supplies
that endpoint. The dimension-one body case is the centered uniform
interval and is direct.

Symmetric independent noise is handled by pairing its scalar values
s and -s, including arbitrary atoms; its zero atom uses the zero-shift
case. No density or finite moment of the noise is needed for the cap
bound. A finite first moment is needed only for calling g the convolution
centroid. The product-body consequence uses genuine independence and
central symmetry of the finite base law; vertical boundaries are counted
in full and have mass at least one half.

All stated conclusions follow. There is no unproved equality
classification, no monotonicity claim for T_d(r), and no extension from
product fibers to a general mixed source in this result.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
